title: Tenali Raman and the Tungabhadra Flood

full_text:
Following unseasonal, torrential cloudbursts in the Western Ghats, the sacred Tungabhadra River rose to alarming heights, threatening to breach the southern earthen bund that protected the low-lying weavers' colony of Vijayanagara.
The royal engineers panicked:
'The stone quarry is ten miles away, and we have no jute sandbags left in the city storehouses! Within four hours, the river will overflow, drowning hundreds of homes and workshops!'

King Krishnadevaraya rode to the riverbank in anguish, watching the swirling muddy torrents erode the earthen levee.

Tenali Raman did not waste a moment in despair. He ran into the nearby textile bazaar, banged a brass gong, and called out to all the weavers and cloth merchants:
'Brothers and sisters! Bring forth every scrap of unsold coarse cotton, torn dhotis, old sarees, and burlap sheets! Our city needs your cloth!'

The weavers responded instantly. Within twenty minutes, mountains of fabric were hauled to the riverbank.
Under Tenali’s energetic direction, hundreds of townsfolk filled the sarees and dhotis with river gravel, clay, and stones, tying the fabric into thousands of tight, resilient sandbags!

Tenali himself stood waist-deep in the cold, rushing water, helping porters stack the heavy fabric sandbags in three overlapping rows against the weakened levee.
Inspired by Tenali’s selfless courage, ministers, soldiers, and artisans joined the chain, heaving sacks until a formidable new barrier fifty cubits long reinforced the levee!

When the midnight flood crest struck, the improvised cotton-and-clay barrier held firm! The angry waters swirled harmlessly against the textile wall and drained into the irrigation canals.
The weavers' colony was saved without the loss of a single life or loom.

The next morning, as the waters receded, King Krishnadevaraya embraced Tenali Raman on the muddy levee:
'Tenali, while my engineers worried about distant stone quarries, thy resourcefulness mobilized the love and labor of our people. Thou hast saved our capital!'
The King ordered all weavers compensated with double the value of their donated cloth, and Tenali was hailed as the Guardian of the River.
moral: Unity, quick improvisation, and selfless community leadership avert catastrophic natural disasters.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Tenali and the Flood"?
options: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
